letters.name: b
letters.memoryTrick: Like an English 'p' but without the puff of air — hold your breath a little. Close your lips and release softly.

letters.name: p
letters.memoryTrick: Like English 'p' in 'park' — a strong puff of air. Hold your hand in front of your mouth and you should feel the burst.

letters.name: m
letters.memoryTrick: Just like English 'm' — press your lips together and hum. Same as humming 'mmm' when something tastes good.

letters.name: f
letters.memoryTrick: Same as English 'f' — top teeth on bottom lip, blow air through. Like blowing out a candle gently.

letters.name: d
letters.memoryTrick: Like an English 't' but softer, with no puff of air. Your tongue tip touches behind your top teeth. Similar to the 't' in 'stop'.

letters.name: t
letters.memoryTrick: Like English 't' in 'top' — with a strong puff of air. Your tongue tip touches behind your top teeth, then releases with a burst.

letters.name: n
letters.memoryTrick: Same as English 'n' — tongue tip on the roof just behind your teeth. Let the sound flow through your nose.

letters.name: l
letters.memoryTrick: Like English 'l' in 'love' — tongue tip touches the roof just behind your teeth, air flows around the sides. Keep it light, not dark like in 'pull'.

letters.name: g
letters.memoryTrick: Like an English 'k' but without the puff of air — like the 'c' in 'score'. Your tongue presses the soft palate at the back.

letters.name: k
letters.memoryTrick: Like English 'k' in 'key' — with a strong puff of air. Hold your hand in front of your mouth to feel the burst.

letters.name: h
letters.memoryTrick: Like the 'ch' in Scottish 'loch' or German 'Bach' — a scratchy sound from the back of your throat. Stronger and rougher than English 'h'.

letters.name: j
letters.memoryTrick: Like the 'j' in 'jeep' but with your tongue flat against the roof of your mouth and lips spread wide like a smile. No puff of air.

letters.name: q
letters.memoryTrick: Like English 'ch' in 'cheese' but with your tongue flat and lips spread in a smile — plus a strong puff of air. NOT like English 'qu'.

letters.name: x
letters.memoryTrick: Like English 'sh' but with your tongue flat behind your lower teeth and lips spread wide in a smile. A hissing sound, sharper than 'sh'. NOT like English 'x'.

letters.name: zh
letters.memoryTrick: Like English 'j' in 'judge' but with your tongue tip curled back. No puff of air. Think of saying 'j' with your tongue pulled back.

letters.name: ch
letters.memoryTrick: Like English 'ch' in 'church' but with your tongue tip curled back, plus a strong puff of air. Think of an exaggerated, breathy 'ch'.

letters.name: sh
letters.memoryTrick: Like English 'sh' in 'shoe' but with your tongue tip curled back towards the roof. A thicker, deeper 'sh' sound.

letters.name: r
letters.memoryTrick: Like a mix of English 'r' and the 's' in 'pleasure' — tongue curled back, buzzing. Similar to 'r' in 'red' but with the tongue tip further back.

letters.name: z
letters.memoryTrick: Like the 'ds' in 'beds' or 'ts' in 'cats' — a quick 'dz' with no puff of air. Your tongue tip touches behind your bottom teeth.

letters.name: c
letters.memoryTrick: Like the 'ts' in 'cats' but with a strong puff of air. Your tongue tip is behind your bottom teeth. Think 'ts!' with an extra breath.

letters.name: s
letters.memoryTrick: Same as English 's' in 'see' — a clean hissing sound. Tongue tip is behind your bottom teeth, unlike English where it's higher.

letters.name: y
letters.memoryTrick: Like English 'y' in 'yes' — a quick glide. When followed by 'i', it's essentially silent but marks the syllable boundary. Think 'yee' without drawing it out.

letters.name: w
letters.memoryTrick: Like English 'w' in 'water' — round your lips tightly. When followed by 'u', it's essentially silent but rounds the syllable. Think 'woo' quickly.

letters.name: a
letters.memoryTrick: Like the 'a' in 'father' — open your mouth wide and let the sound out. Relaxed and open, not like the 'a' in 'cat'.

letters.name: o
letters.memoryTrick: Like the 'o' in 'more' but with rounded lips and no 'r' coloring. Pure, round, and held steady — think of saying 'oh!' in surprise.

letters.name: e
letters.memoryTrick: Like the 'u' in 'fur' but without the 'r' — your tongue is pulled back and mid-height. Similar to saying 'uh' while smiling slightly.

letters.name: i
letters.memoryTrick: Like the 'ee' in 'see' — spread your lips wide like you're smiling. Keep it tense and high in your mouth. A clean, bright 'ee' sound.

letters.name: u
letters.memoryTrick: Like the 'oo' in 'boot' — round your lips tightly into a small circle. Hold it steady without letting it slide into a 'w' at the end.

letters.name: ü (u-umlaut)
letters.memoryTrick: Say 'ee' (like in 'see') but round your lips tightly as if saying 'oo'. It's exactly the French 'u' in 'tu' or German 'ü' in 'grün'.

letters.name: ai
letters.memoryTrick: Like the 'igh' in 'sigh' or 'eye' — start with 'a' as in 'father' and glide quickly to 'ee'. But shorter than English; don't draw it out.

letters.name: ei
letters.memoryTrick: Like the 'ay' in 'day' — start with a mid 'e' and glide quickly to 'ee'. A smooth, short glide. Similar to the Canadian 'eh'.

letters.name: ao
letters.memoryTrick: Like the 'ow' in 'cow' — start with 'a' as in 'father' and glide to 'oo'. But less drawn out than English; make it snappy.

letters.name: ou
letters.memoryTrick: Like the 'o' in 'go' — start with 'o' and glide quickly to 'oo'. Keep your lips rounded throughout. Think of the 'oh' in 'oh no'.

letters.name: an
letters.memoryTrick: Like 'ahn' — 'a' as in 'father' followed by 'n'. But the 'a' is more fronted than in English 'on'. Think of saying 'Ann' with a British accent.

letters.name: en
letters.memoryTrick: Like the 'en' in 'taken' — a relaxed, neutral vowel followed by 'n'. Similar to 'un' in 'fun' but softer and more central.

letters.name: ang
letters.memoryTrick: Like 'ahng' — 'a' as in 'father' followed by the 'ng' in 'sing'. Open your mouth wider than for English 'ong'. It's a big, open sound.

letters.name: eng
letters.memoryTrick: Like the 'ung' in 'sung' — a relaxed middle vowel followed by 'ng'. Similar to the 'eng' in 'length' but with more nasal resonance.

letters.name: ong
letters.memoryTrick: Like 'oong' — round your lips and follow with 'ng'. Similar to the 'ong' in 'song' but with more rounded lips at the start. Think 'oh-ng' quickly.

letters.name: er
letters.memoryTrick: Like the 'er' in 'her' (American accent) — a curled-back tongue with a vocalic 'r'. This is a retroflex sound; your tongue tip curls up and back. It's its own syllable.

letters.name: ia
letters.memoryTrick: Like 'yah' — a quick 'y' glide into 'a' as in 'father'. Think of the 'ya' in 'yacht' but crisper.

letters.name: ie
letters.memoryTrick: Like 'yeah' — a quick 'y' glide into a mid-front 'e'. Similar to the 'ye' in 'yes' but ending more open. Think 'yeh' with spread lips.

letters.name: iao
letters.memoryTrick: Like 'yow' — a quick 'y' glide into 'ow' as in 'cow'. Think of saying 'meow' without the 'm'. A three-part glide: yee-ah-oo, blended fast.

words.meaning: strip; measure word for long things

letters.name: iu (iou)
letters.memoryTrick: Like 'yo' in 'yo-yo' — a quick 'y' glide into 'oh'. Despite the spelling 'iu', it's actually 'iou' compressed. Think 'yo' but with slightly rounded lips at the end.

letters.name: ian
letters.memoryTrick: Like 'yen' — a quick 'y' glide into 'en'. The 'a' is higher and more fronted than in plain 'an', closer to the 'e' in 'bed'. Think 'yen' (Japanese money) but crisper.

letters.name: in
letters.memoryTrick: Like 'een' — 'ee' as in 'see' followed directly by 'n'. Keep your tongue high and front throughout, then close with the 'n'. Think 'inn' but with a smile.

letters.name: iang
letters.memoryTrick: Like 'yahng' — a quick 'y' glide into 'ang'. Think 'young' but with a wide-open 'ah' instead of 'uh'. A big, bright nasal sound.

letters.name: ing
letters.memoryTrick: Like 'eeng' — 'ee' as in 'see' followed by 'ng' as in 'sing'. Keep your tongue high and smile, then close the nasal at the back. Think 'ing' in 'sing' but with a purer 'ee'.

letters.name: iong
letters.memoryTrick: Like 'yoong' — a quick 'y' glide into 'ong'. Think 'young' with rounded lips throughout. Your tongue starts high and front, then slides back for the 'ng'.

letters.name: ua
letters.memoryTrick: Like 'wah' — a quick 'w' glide into 'a' as in 'father'. Round your lips at the start, then open wide. Think of a baby saying 'wah!'.

letters.name: uo
letters.memoryTrick: Like 'waw' — a quick 'w' glide into 'o'. Round your lips and hold the roundedness through the vowel. Similar to the 'wa' in 'water' but ending in a pure 'o'.

letters.name: uai
letters.memoryTrick: Like 'why' — a quick 'w' glide into 'ai' (eye). Round your lips, then glide through 'ah' to 'ee'. Think of asking 'why?' but with more rounded lips at the start.

letters.name: ui (uei)
letters.memoryTrick: Like 'way' — a quick 'w' glide into 'ei' (ay). Round your lips at the start, then spread into a smile for the 'ay' glide. Think of the word 'way'.

letters.name: uan
letters.memoryTrick: Like 'wahn' — a quick 'w' glide into 'an'. Round your lips at the start, then open to 'ah' and close with 'n'. Think 'one' but with a British-style broad 'ah'.

letters.name: un (uen)
letters.memoryTrick: Like 'wun' — a quick 'w' glide into 'en'. Round your lips at the start, then relax into the neutral vowel and close with 'n'. Think 'one' said quickly.

letters.name: uang
letters.memoryTrick: Like 'wahng' — a quick 'w' glide into 'ang'. Round your lips, then open wide for the 'ah' and close with 'ng'. Think 'wong' but with a much wider, more open vowel.

letters.name: ueng
letters.memoryTrick: Like 'wung' — a quick 'w' glide into 'eng'. Round your lips, relax into the mid vowel, then close with 'ng'. This final only appears as a standalone syllable 'weng', never with other initials.

letters.name: üe
letters.memoryTrick: Say 'ü' (ee with rounded lips), then glide quickly to a mid-front 'e' like the 'e' in 'bed'. Think of the French 'yeux' but shorter.

letters.name: üan
letters.memoryTrick: Say 'ü' (ee with rounded lips), then glide into 'en' as in 'hen'. Keep your lips rounded at the start, then relax. Think 'you-en' said quickly with rounded-lip 'ee'.

letters.name: ün
letters.memoryTrick: Say 'ü' (ee with rounded lips), then close with 'n'. Keep your tongue high and front throughout. Think of saying 'een' with rounded lips — a French-style nasal 'une'.

letters.name: Tone 1 (High Level)
letters.memoryTrick: High and steady, like a singer holding one note. Keep your pitch flat and high throughout the syllable — as if you're a robot saying 'beeep'. Symbol: a flat bar above the vowel (ā).

letters.name: Tone 2 (Rising)
letters.memoryTrick: Rises from the middle to high, like asking a question in English: 'What?' or 'Huh?' Your voice climbs up smoothly — like a plane taking off. Symbol: an upward-slanting bar (á).

letters.name: Tone 3 (Falling-Rising)
letters.memoryTrick: Dips low then rises — like your voice when you're doubtful and say 'Weeell...' It starts mid, dips down deep (almost creaky), then comes back up. Symbol: a V-shaped mark (ǎ).

letters.name: Tone 4 (Falling)
letters.memoryTrick: Drops sharply from high to low, like saying 'No!' firmly or giving a command. Short, forceful, and decisive — like stomping your foot. Symbol: a downward-slanting bar (à).

letters.name: Neutral Tone
letters.memoryTrick: Light, short, and unstressed — like the second syllable in 'sofa' or the 'a' in 'about'. No tone mark is written. Just say it quickly and lightly, letting the previous tone set the pitch.
